correctness.rationale: The unordered cosine values are precisely the roots of 4X³−3X−c=0. For |c|<1, differentiating the symmetric sum gives b/4 times the second divided difference of x↦g′(a+bx), so the derivative has the sign of g‴. With g(u)=exp(eu), g(u)=exp(−eu), and g(u)=log(1−exp(−eu)), the signs are +, −, +, respectively. Applying these to the exactly-one probability, expected richness and all-three probability gives the stated strict increase in c; the complement of zero-or-one and then subtraction give the two strict decreases. The no-detection probability is exp(−3ae), independent of phase. Continuity at the repeated roots gives strict order up to the endpoints, and a phase-independent efficiency mixture preserves strictness because e>0 has positive probability. Direct endpoint substitution gives the stated contrast. Its logarithmic derivative decreases strictly from +∞ to b−2a<0, and the expansion at zero gives b³e³/4. The maximizing phase congruences follow from the endpoints of cos(3θ).
residual_risks: The numerical replay corroborates one example, not the theorem. The effort optimum is for deterministic effort and for the contrast, not absolute detection or arbitrary mixtures.

value.rationale: The exact order shows why a season that is optimal for expected richness or detection of all three can be worst for detection of at least two, even when shared sampling quality is random. This supplies a concrete design distinction that cannot be obtained merely by comparing mean intensity, which is constant when summed. The effort contrast quantifies when that design choice matters most under the model.
residual_risks: Idealized symmetric model, not a field-calibrated result or occupancy theorem. No implication claimed for non-equidistant phases, phase-dependent efficiency or arbitrary survey dates.
